report.tagline: An online marketplace where millions of people and small shops sell used, collectible and new items to buyers around the world.
report.simpleSummary: eBay is a giant online flea market. Anyone can list an old phone, a trading card or a car part, and buyers either bid in an auction or pay a fixed price. eBay does not own the stock. It takes a cut when something sells and charges sellers to show their items higher in search.

overview.whatItDoes: eBay connects people who want to sell things with people who want to buy them. It is strongest in items you cannot easily find new: trading cards, sneakers, vintage watches, car parts and refurbished phones. It makes money from fees on each sale and from ads sellers buy inside eBay.
howItWorks: A seller lists an item with photos, a price or an auction start, and a shipping option. eBay's AI tool Magical Listing can write the title and details from a photo.
Buyers find it through search or eBay's app feed, then bid or click Buy It Now.
eBay collects the payment through Managed Payments and pays the seller after taking its fees.
For high-value items like sneakers, watches and graded cards, the Authenticity Guarantee sends the item to an expert checker before it reaches the buyer.
The eBay Money Back Guarantee refunds buyers if an item never arrives or is not as described.
Newer formats include eBay Live, a live-stream shopping show, and the eBay Vault, where collectors store cards and trade them without shipping.
overview.valueProposition: For buyers: the widest choice of used, rare and collectible items, with a refund promise. For sellers: access to about 136 million buyers without building their own shop.

painPoints.pain: Rare or used items are hard to find in normal shops.

painPoints.pain: Buyers fear fakes on expensive items.
painPoints.howSolved: Authenticity Guarantee checks sneakers, watches, handbags and graded cards before delivery.

painPoints.pain: Buyers fear paying and getting nothing.
painPoints.howSolved: eBay Money Back Guarantee and payments held by eBay.

painPoints.pain: Sellers have no audience of their own.
painPoints.howSolved: eBay brings the buyers and handles search, payment and dispute tools.

painPoints.pain: Listing an item takes too long.
painPoints.howSolved: Magical Listing fills in titles, item details and price suggestions from a photo.

painPoints.pain: Shipping cards and small items is costly and confusing.

coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Lower effort means more casual sellers list, which grows supply.

businessModel.summary: eBay makes money in two main ways: a final value fee on each sale, and ads that sellers buy to rank higher. It holds no stock, so it is cheap to run and very profitable, but it must keep both buyers and sellers happy.

revenueStreams.detail: About 13.6% of the total sale price in most US categories, plus about $0.30 to $0.40 per order. Lower rates for some high-value items.
Sellers pay a chosen percentage of the sale price when a promoted item sells. About $575 million in Q3 2026.
Margins on shipping labels, international shipping and payment processing.
In the UK, private sellers pay no selling fee since 2024; buyers pay a buyer protection fee instead.
Depop, TCGplayer and Goldin earn their own fees.

businessModel.pricing: Free to list up to 250 items a month in the US. Final value fee of about 13.6% for most categories plus a per-order fee. Store subscriptions from about $5 to $3,000 a month. Promoted Listings rates are set by the seller.
costDrivers: Sales and marketing, about $747 million in Q3 2026
Customer support and buyer refunds under the Money Back Guarantee
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a $100 card sale in the US, eBay keeps about $14 in final value fees. If the seller used a 5% Promoted Listings rate, eBay keeps another $5. That is about $19, or a take rate (eBay's share of each sale) near 19% on that item. Card payment costs take about $2 to $3 of that. Because eBay owns no stock and no warehouses for most items, most of the rest is gross profit, which is why its operating margin sits near 19 to 20%.

howTheyGetUsers: Google search and shopping ads, since many eBay listings rank for rare item names
Focus categories like collectibles, motors parts and pre-loved luxury, marketed to fans directly
Buying other marketplaces: Depop (closed July 2026), Tise, TCGplayer and Goldin
eBay Live shows that turn viewers into bidders
Removing seller fees for UK private sellers to win back casual sellers from Vinted
whatBringsUsersBack: Saved searches and price alerts for items collectors want
Auctions ending at set times create urgency
Items held in the eBay Vault that can be resold with one tap
Sellers return because their buyers are on eBay
growth.moat: eBay has 30 years of buyers and sellers for odd, rare and used items. A collector goes where the most rare cards are listed, and a seller lists where the most collectors are. This two-sided network effect, plus sold-price history and authentication centres, is hard for a new site to copy.

competitors.name: Amazon
competitors.positioning: New items with fast Prime delivery.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: eBay wins on used, rare and collectible items and auctions, not speed.

competitors.name: Whatnot
competitors.positioning: Live-stream shopping app for cards and collectibles.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: eBay has far more listed stock and buyers; Whatnot leads in live shows. eBay Live is the response.

competitors.name: Vinted
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: eBay covers all categories; Vinted is simpler and cheaper for casual clothing sellers.

competitors.name: Facebook Marketplace
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: eBay offers shipping, payments and buyer protection across the country.

competitors.name: Temu and Shein
competitors.positioning: Very cheap new goods shipped from China.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: eBay is moving away from cheap new goods toward items Temu cannot sell, like collectibles and used goods.

northStar.metric: Number of successful transactions per month where the buyer did not open a dispute
northStar.why: Each clean transaction means a buyer found what they wanted and a seller got paid. It grows with both sides of the marketplace, and it punishes fakes and bad experiences, unlike raw GMV.

guardrailMetrics: Seller net payout as a share of sale price (fees must not creep up so far that sellers leave)
Search result relevance score, so more ads do not bury the best match
strengths: Deep supply of rare and used items that new rivals lack
High margins because it holds no stock
Strong position in collectibles, with TCGplayer, Goldin, the Vault and authentication
Big ad business on top of fees
Healthy cash flow funds about $2 billion of buybacks a year
weaknesses: Organic buyer growth is close to zero, about 1% in Q3 2026
Old, cluttered user interface that feels dated next to Vinted or Depop
Heavy reliance on trading cards, which may cool
Sellers feel they must pay for ads to be seen
risks: Whatnot and TikTok Shop winning live shopping
Vinted taking casual clothing sellers in the UK and US
A crash in trading card prices would hit eBay's fastest-growing category
Tax reporting rules (such as US 1099-K thresholds) scaring off casual sellers
Cheap new goods from Temu and Shein pulling bargain buyers away

Payout holds and account limits for new sellers
Customer support is hard to reach and often scripted
Magical Listing makes errors that sellers must fix
Cluttered search full of sponsored items

improvementIdeas.idea: Seller return-fraud shield: photo check-in on returns for items over $100, with eBay covering losses if the returned item does not match.
improvementIdeas.problem: Sellers lose money to buyers who return a different or broken item.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher seller trust and fewer sellers quitting focus categories.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Seller churn after a lost return case

improvementIdeas.idea: Show sellers an 'organic reach' score before they pick an ad rate, with a free boost for first 10 listings.
improvementIdeas.problem: New sellers feel they must pay for ads to get any sales.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More new sellers make a first sale and stay.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: New seller first-sale rate in 30 days

improvementIdeas.idea: One-tap cross-listing from eBay to Depop for fashion items, and showing Depop items in eBay search.
improvementIdeas.problem: eBay struggles with young fashion buyers while owning Depop.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More supply and buyers in fashion across both apps.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Fashion GMV growth among buyers under 30

improvementIdeas.idea: Simplified 'new buyer' home screen focused on trending categories and guaranteed items.
improvementIdeas.problem: Organic buyer growth is flat, and new visitors find the site cluttered.

improvementIdeas.idea: Card price alerts tied to Vault holdings, suggesting when to sell.
improvementIdeas.problem: Vault cards sit idle, and collectors miss price peaks.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More trades per Vault item and more fees.

pmLessons: When you cannot win the whole market, pick niches where you are strong. eBay grew by focusing on collectibles and used goods rather than fighting Amazon on new items.
Ads can become a second business, but too many ads hurt search quality and anger sellers. Watch guardrail metrics.
Trust features like authentication unlock high-value categories. Spending on trust can be a growth lever.
Buying growth through acquisitions, like Depop, can hide weak organic growth. Always look at numbers without acquisitions.
In a two-sided marketplace, pricing changes for one side affect the other. Free UK selling moved costs to buyers.

interviewQuestions.question: eBay's active buyers grow only 1% without acquisitions. How would you grow them?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment buyers: new, lapsed, enthusiasts. Find the biggest drop-off in the funnel. Pick one segment, suggest two or three ideas, and define a success metric and guardrail.

interviewQuestions.question: Should eBay remove seller fees in the US like it did for UK private sellers?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare pros (more supply, beat Vinted) and cons (revenue loss, buyer fee pushback). Model the revenue hit and needed volume lift. Suggest a test in one category.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you measure the success of eBay Live?
interviewQuestions.hint: North star like live GMV per viewer hour. Inputs: shows, viewers, bid rate, repeat viewers. Guardrails: dispute rate, impact on regular listings.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to reduce fakes in sneakers below the $150 Authenticity Guarantee threshold.
interviewQuestions.hint: Define the user and the risk. Options: AI photo checks, seller trust scores, optional paid check. Pick one, weigh cost per item against fraud loss.

interviewQuestions.question: Sellers say Promoted Listings are mandatory to get sales. What do you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Check data on organic versus paid sales. Balance ad revenue against seller trust and search quality. Propose transparency or caps, with metrics on both sides.

assumptions: The $100 card sale example uses the standard US fee of about 13.6% plus a $0.40 order fee; real fees vary by category and seller level.
Payment processing cost of $2 to $3 per $100 is an estimate based on typical card fees.
The 'about 2 billion live listings' figure is eBay's long-stated number and may have changed.
Active seller count is not disclosed by eBay; the last official figure was 17 million in 2021.
